subject: SLA uptime calculation dispute — Feb 26 incident and maintenance overlap
messages:
From: Michael Torres <michael.torres@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@acme-corp.com, procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dispute: downtime counted against SLA for Feb 26

Hi Marissa,

We reviewed Redwood's status post for Feb 26 and your uptime report. The status page shows an 'outage' between 2026-02-26T21:58Z and 2026-02-26T22:45Z. Our finance and procurement teams are saying that those 47 minutes should be counted against the monthly SLA window and trigger a credit per section 4.2 of our contract.

However, your team previously notified us of a scheduled maintenance window for Feb 26 between 23:00-23:30 UTC — which does not overlap our observed outage. Can you explain why the incident is being presented as maintenance-window-related in your report? We need a formal calculation of downtime and the statutory credit amount by EOD Friday so procurement can process the credit request.

Thanks,
Michael Torres
Head of Platform Operations
Acme Payments

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Torres <michael.torres@acme.com>
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dispute: downtime counted against SLA for Feb 26

Hi Michael — thanks for flagging this.

I'm escalating to our SRE and support team to verify the timestamps and root cause. I see why this looks concerning from your side; we'll pull the raw logs and correlation data (latency histograms, error rates, and routing events) and get back with a precise uptime calculation and whether any portion falls inside a pre-announced maintenance window.

Looping in Dylan (support) for the technical details and Markus (infra) for the kernel-level routing notes. I will follow up with an interim update within 24 hours and a final response no later than Friday COB.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Torres <michael.torres@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dispute: downtime counted against SLA for Feb 26 — technical summary attached

Hi Michael —

Thanks for the patience. Attached are the log extracts and timeline (redwood_incident_log_20260226.zip) and an interim summary (interim_incident_summary_20260303.pdf). High-level points:

- Timeline (UTC):
  - 2026-02-26T21:50:12Z — Upstream DB vendor reports degraded region (publicly reported).
  - 2026-02-26T21:58:34Z — We started observing elevated 5xx rates and tail latency on the serving cluster handling Acme traffic.
  - 2026-02-26T22:00:00Z — Automated request routing attempted failover to cold capacity; some requests saw increased latency or transient errors during routing and KV cache warmup.
  - 2026-02-26T22:30:45Z — Error rate largely recovered after fallback to alternate provider path.
  - 2026-02-26T23:00:00Z — Scheduled maintenance window (announced) began for unrelated infra compaction; it ended at 23:30:00Z.

- Impact: For the period 21:58:34Z — 22:30:45Z (~32 minutes) we recorded a partial degradation for Acme's routes: 12.1% of requests returned 5xx and 27% of requests saw >2x baseline latency. Importantly the maintenance window at 23:00Z did not overlap with the initial degradation window.

- Uptime calculation per our SLA: we compute "unavailable time" as full-request failures plus minutes where P99 tail-latency exceeds the configured SLO threshold for a customer route. The automated routing that occurred because of the DB vendor issue produced a period of partial degradation that meets the SLA definition for "service unavailability" for certain request classes.

We'll include the raw histograms in the zip for your team's verification. If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute ride-along with our SREs tomorrow morning to walk through the logs.

Apologies for the disruption — the root cause traces back to the third-party DB provider and our failover path executed but caused noticeable latency for a minority of requests.

Regards,
Dylan Brooks
Support Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Michael Torres <michael.torres@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@acme-corp.com, procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 08:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dispute: downtime counted against SLA for Feb 26 — request for formal credit calculation

Marissa / Dylan —

Thanks for the initial timeline. I appreciate the breakdown but Acme finance needs two things to proceed: (1) a clear statement if the 21:58–22:30 window is being counted as "downtime" under the SLA (not just "partial degradation"), and (2) the exact credit amount and mechanism (line-item credit vs. invoice adjustment). Your statement about P99 thresholds isn't sufficient for procurement; they want the numeric minutes that will be applied.

To be clear, our status page recorded the customer-visible impact as 21:58–22:45. If you are calculating 21:58–22:30, we need the evidence for the truncated end time. Also, if the root cause is a third-party vendor, contract section 4.5 indicates those events can still be counted unless specifically excluded by an exception. Please confirm.

Michael

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Acme dispute — need legal & infra input on SLA minute calc

Team —

Acme is pressing for a formal credit calculation and wants documentation they can pass to procurement. Key points: they see 21:58–22:45 on their side; our interim shows recovery at 22:30:45. They question whether third-party vendor outages can be excluded from SLA.

Can legal confirm contract language on third-party exclusions (stephanie) and infra confirm whether any post-22:30 errors were client-visible (markus)? If we accept the 32 minutes as "unavailable," we should prepare an offer (provisional credit) while we finish the RCA. I want to avoid a procurement escalation.

If possible, can we produce a short customer-facing calculation table and apply a 10% service credit per the SLA for the affected billing month as a gesture while the RCA completes?

Thanks — Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Torres <michael.torres@acme.com>
Cc: ops@acme-corp.com, procurement@acme-corp.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Final calculation and credit for Feb 26 incident

Hi Michael —

Thank you again for your patience while we completed the verification. Below is the formal calculation and next steps:

Summary:
- Observed customer-visible impact window (Redwood verified): 2026-02-26T21:58:34Z — 2026-02-26T22:30:45Z (32 minutes, 11 seconds). Our detailed histograms and request-level logs are attached in final_incident_report_20260305.pdf.
- Acme's status showing 21:58–22:45 reflects a longer tail of client-side retransmits — our server-side telemetry indicates recovery by 22:30:45 when 5xx and elevated tail-latency dropped below SLA thresholds. We included the per-minute P99 and error-rate table in the report for audit.
- Contract interpretation: per section 4.5 (SLA exceptions), third-party vendor failures are not automatically excluded. Exceptions require demonstrable customer routing changes or agreed-upon maintenance windows. This event was caused by an upstream DB vendor degradation; therefore it is counted toward Redwood's availability metrics.

Credit calculation applied:
- Affected minutes counted: 32
- Monthly uptime impact: (32 minutes / (30 days * 24 * 60)) = ~0.074% for the billing month.
- Per our SLA, the incident qualifies for a 10% service credit for the affected month (nearest term in contract). We will apply a 10% credit to your March invoice as a line-item adjustment.

What we did for you:
- Applied a provisional 10% service credit to invoice ACME-2026-03 (you will see a line-item: "SLA credit — Feb 26 incident — $0.00"; finance will process the numeric adjustment).
- Attached final incident report (final_incident_report_20260305.pdf) and raw extracts (redwood_incident_log_20260226.zip) for your records.
- Action items: our infra team (Markus) will continue to work with the DB provider to harden failover paths; Dylan is assigning a follow-up post-mortem call (proposed: Tue, 3/9 10:00 UTC) to walk through the logs and remediation plan.

If Acme needs a signed credit acknowledgement for procurement, I can route a DocuSign credit memo by EOD Friday. Please confirm if that is required.

Apologies again for the disruption — we value Acme as a strategic customer and want to ensure transparency.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
